purchasePathNote: Apollo is not sold publicly. Apptronik works with enterprise partners such as Mercedes-Benz and asks companies to use its contact form.

configurations.name: Apollo (2023 cost goal)
configurations.notes: IEEE Spectrum (2023-01-27) reported the goal of a platform that costs 'well under US $100,000'. A ceiling stated as a goal, not a price.

configurations.name: Apollo (long-term target)
configurations.notes: CEO Jeff Cardenas discusses making a safe, reliable humanoid 'for less than $50,000' (podcast, 2025-02-20). Long-term goal, not a price.

sellers.name: Apptronik (official)
sellers.offers: No public price; 'Get Started' contact form for companies.

faq.a: Not as a public product. Apptronik has no price or order page and directs companies to a contact form.
Apptronik has not published a price. In 2023 the company's goal was a platform costing well under US$100,000, and CEO Jeff Cardenas has talked about getting a humanoid below $50,000.
Apptronik announced a commercial agreement with Mercedes-Benz to pilot Apollo in its factories.

notes: Both prices are company goals, not quotes. Some sites cite a CEO interview with IEEE Spectrum in August 2023 for the $50,000 figure; that article was not found, so the podcast is used instead.
researchNotes: The apptronik.com/apollo page used in the evidence pack now returns 404; the current product page is apptronik.com/apollo/apollo-2.
